Apply Supplied Group Thresholds to Observations

Source: R/grouped-thresholds.R
ApplyGroupedThresholds.Rd

Looks up one supplied threshold per composite group and tests strictly greater than. Thresholds are not estimated; equality is FALSE. Eligibility and numeric availability remain explicit. No labels, units or observation universe are inferred. Unknown groups fail, including groups of ineligible observations.

Usage

ApplyGroupedThresholds(
  data,
  thresholds,
  groups,
  id,
  value,
  threshold,
  eligible
)

Arguments

data

Data frame of observations. Original columns, metadata and row order are preserved; inputs are not mutated.

thresholds

Data frame with one threshold per unique group. Extra groups are permitted. Supply an explicit NA threshold for an unavailable group.

groups

Nonempty plain character vector of distinct group column names.

id

Plain character scalar naming the observation ID column. Identity is unique within groups; IDs may recur across different groups.

value

Plain character scalar naming the observation value column.

threshold

Plain character scalar naming the supplied threshold column. Selected numeric columns must be plain integer/double, finite or NA; classed, dimensional, complex, NaN and infinite values fail even when ineligible.

eligible

Plain character scalar naming a plain logical eligibility column. TRUE, FALSE and NA are distinct. Data roles must not overlap; threshold must not overlap groups. Keys are plain nonblank character values without NA or ASCII 28. Selectors are dimensionless and nonblank.

Value

A data frame with all original observation columns unchanged, followed by threshold_value (double), threshold_available and value_available (logical), above_threshold (logical or NA), and threshold_status (character). Original columns with these reserved names fail. Status precedence is INELIGIBLE, UNKNOWN_ELIGIBILITY, MISSING_VALUE_AND_THRESHOLD, MISSING_THRESHOLD, MISSING_VALUE, COMPLETE. Availability flags retain numeric missingness independently of eligibility. Only eligible observations with both numbers known receive a comparison. Empty inputs retain typed outputs; nonempty observations require complete group-reference coverage. Metadata classes and the original value storage type are preserved. Units must agree upstream; no conversion is performed.

Examples

d <- data.frame(group = "a", id = c("x", "y"), value = c(1, 2), eligible = TRUE)
r <- data.frame(group = "a", cutoff = 1)
ApplyGroupedThresholds(d, r, "group", "id", "value", "cutoff", "eligible")
#>   group id value eligible threshold_value threshold_available value_available
#> 1     a  x     1     TRUE               1                TRUE            TRUE
#> 2     a  y     2     TRUE               1                TRUE            TRUE
#>   above_threshold threshold_status
#> 1           FALSE         COMPLETE
#> 2            TRUE         COMPLETE
